changed.what: 2012 -> 2011; patient side first public at the EASL late-breaker of 2 Apr 2011 (Lok et al., abstract 1356, J Hepatol 2011;54 S1: 4/11 dual, 10/10 quad SVR12; natap.org/2011/EASL/EASL_28.htm); model side Gao 2010 already public; status same unchanged

2014 -> 2013; ledipasvir's own first use of replicon RAS phenotyping is Wong 2013 (AAC, PMID 23877691, epub 2013-07-22: patient-derived M28T/Q30R/L31M/Y93C phenotyped in replicons); proxy, earlier congress posters not checked
2015 -> 2010; daclatasvir's own first use of the RAS replicon is 2010 (Fridell 2010 AAC, PMID 20585111, epub 2010-06-28; Gao 2010 Nature, epub 2010-04-21), not a 2015 placeholder

2016 -> 2013; elbasvir (MK-8742) first public replicon use is Coburn 2013 (ChemMedChem, PMID 24127258, epub 2013-10-14), whose design goal was potency against NS5A resistance mutations; proxy, variant table not read (abstract only)

2020 -> 2018; the prospective modeling pilot (NCT03603327) was first public at the AASLD late-breaker LB-34, Nov 2018 (Etzion et al., Hepatology 2018;68(6):1468A), which names sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, elbasvir/grazoprevir, sofosbuvir/ledipasvir and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir as the regimens modeled
